topStories.headline: Presidio Counts Down to Its 250th Birthday — Documentary Premiere Set for September 17
topStories.dek: The Presidio of San Francisco marks 250 years since its founding with a landmark film screening and champagne reception on the exact anniversary date.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Presidio is approaching one of its most significant milestones: the 250th anniversary of the founding of El Presidio de San Francisco on September 17, 1776. The park has spent the year programming events tied to that date, and the centerpiece evening is now confirmed — a world premiere film screening at the 600-seat Presidio Theatre on September 17.

The Presidio Historical Association and the San Francisco Historical Society will co-present the world premiere of 'Documenting Anza by Bike,' a feature documentary chronicling Professor Luis Valle's 1,200-mile bicycle journey retracing Juan Bautista de Anza's original expedition route from Sonora, Mexico, to San Francisco. Doors open at 5:30 p.m., with the screening to be followed by a champagne reception celebrating the park's birthday.

The anniversary also coincides with the America 250 national initiative commemorating the founding of the United States. As the Presidio Trust has noted, El Presidio de San Francisco was founded the same year the Declaration of Independence was signed on the East Coast, giving San Francisco its own 1776 story to tell. The park's story spans millennia and cultures — from the Ramaytush Ohlone people who lived on the land for thousands of years, to Spanish and Mexican colonists, to the U.S. Army, and now to the millions of visitors who explore it as a national park.

Tickets for the September 17 film screening are available at presidiotheatre.org. Admission to the park's ongoing exhibitions and trails remains free.

topStories.headline: Rose Pizzeria Brings Its NYT-Acclaimed Pies to Clement Street
topStories.dek: Berkeley's celebrated Rose Pizzeria has opened its first San Francisco location in the Inner Richmond, arriving to reservations already booked out weeks in advance.
topStories.body:
The Inner Richmond's food corridor gained a headline anchor this spring when Rose Pizzeria — the Berkeley restaurant that The New York Times named one of America's 22 best pizzerias — opened its first San Francisco location at 1 Clement Street, in the former Village Pizzeria space at Arguello Boulevard.

Owner couple Gerad Gobel and Alexis Rorabaugh spent nearly two years calling real estate agents before finally securing a 20-year lease on the prominent corner. The space has been transformed: workers pulled up old tiles to restore an original green-and-white checkered floor, painted most walls green, and installed one back panel of pastoral wallpaper depicting Aventine Hill in Rome. The 44-seat dining room features marble-topped tables and a swirled green marble counter looking into the open kitchen, with about 15 outdoor seats along Arguello.

The San Francisco location is deliberately more expansive than the intimate Berkeley original. The larger kitchen allows for customizable pies for the first time, with diners able to add toppings like mushrooms, sausage, pepperoni, or pickled chiles. The restaurant is open daily for lunch and dinner, sitting directly across from the Sunday Clement Street Farmers Market — already making it a destination for the neighborhood's weekend morning crowd.

Rose Pizzeria opened to no available reservations for weeks. For those who can't book ahead, the restaurant operates on a walk-in basis during off-peak hours. Hours are Monday through Sunday, 11:30 a.m. to 9 p.m.

topStories.headline: Richmond Review Loses Its Founding Editor — And Rallies to Carry On
topStories.dek: Michael Durand, publisher and editor-in-chief of the Richmond Review and Sunset Beacon newspapers, died in May; the papers he built continue to serve the west-side neighborhoods.
topStories.body:
Michael Durand, the founder and longtime publisher and editor-in-chief of the Richmond Review and Sunset Beacon newspapers, passed away on May 30 following a diagnosis of metastatic melanoma, his paper reported this month. Durand built the two community publications into enduring institutions serving the Richmond and Sunset districts, with a combined print circulation of 18,000 copies distributed door-to-door across the west side of San Francisco.

The newspapers — and their companion website, RichmondSunsetNews.com — continue to publish under new editorial stewardship. The loss comes at a moment of broader strain for local news: California has shed a quarter of its newspapers and half its newsroom staff over the past fifteen years, and San Francisco has lost more than half of its neighborhood papers in roughly the same period.

Readers and community members who want to support the Richmond Review and Sunset Beacon can contribute through the paper's website. The publications are among the few remaining independent outlets covering hyperlocal news across the Richmond, from Clement Street merchants to Presidio policy to Ocean Beach conditions — a role that Durand built over decades and that the staff now works to sustain in his memory.

events.title: EXCLUSION Exhibition: The Presidio's Role in WWII Japanese American Incarceration
events.location: Presidio Officers' Club, 50 Moraga Avenue, Presidio
events.description: This award-winning free exhibition, presented by the Presidio Trust with the Fred T. Korematsu Institute and the National Japanese American Historical Society, examines the Presidio's role in the unjust incarceration of 120,000 Japanese Americans during World War II. Open Fridays through Sundays through August 31.

events.title: ArtSeed's 20th Annual Open Call Exhibition: 'So What Now?'
events.location: China Brotsky and Seed Galleries, 1012 Torney Ave, Presidio
events.description: ArtSeed's landmark 20th annual open call exhibition features work by students in the Fine Arts Summer Intensive alongside art created in response to pieces by children from Gaza's Academies of Hope; the closing reception is Friday, September 18, 5–7 p.m., free and open to the public.

events.title: The Etruscans: From the Heart of Ancient Italy
events.location: Legion of Honor, 100 34th Ave, Outer Richmond
events.description: The Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco present the most comprehensive Etruscan exhibition ever staged outside Italy, featuring nearly 200 artifacts including bronze sculptures, gold jewelry, and ceramics — including the Liver of Piacenza, shown outside its place of discovery for the first time.
events.sourceName: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco

events.title: Clement Street Farmers Market
events.location: Clement St between 2nd and 4th Avenues, Inner Richmond
events.description: San Francisco's beloved year-round certified farmers market fills three city blocks of Clement Street every Sunday with fresh produce, baked goods, flowers, and specialty food vendors; CalFresh EBT/SNAP, Market Match, and WIC are accepted.

events.title: World Arts West Dance Festival at Presidio Tunnel Tops
events.location: East Meadow, Presidio Tunnel Tops, Presidio
events.description: The 2026 World Arts West Dance Festival returns to the East Meadow of Presidio Tunnel Tops for an afternoon of free live dance performances and interactive dance workshops, celebrating dance traditions from around the world.

events.title: The Walt Disney Family Museum: The Big Draw Festival
events.location: Walt Disney Family Museum, 104 Montgomery St, Presidio
events.description: The Walt Disney Family Museum celebrates The Big Draw, the world's largest drawing festival, with special programming inviting visitors of all ages to draw, create, and explore animation; museum admission applies.

events.title: Presidio 250th Birthday: 'Documenting Anza by Bike' World Premiere
events.description: On the exact 250th anniversary of the Presidio's founding, the Presidio Historical Association and the San Francisco Historical Society present the world premiere of 'Documenting Anza by Bike,' a documentary following Professor Luis Valle's 1,200-mile bicycle retracing of Anza's expedition; a champagne reception follows the screening.

events.title: Richmond District Cleanup — Internet Archive
events.location: Internet Archive, 300 Funston Ave, Inner Richmond
events.description: Civic Joy Fund hosts a neighborhood cleanup in the Richmond District, mobilizing volunteers to tidy streets and public spaces; participants should register in advance at the Civic Joy Fund Mobilize page.

moreNews.headline: Pacific Café, Outer Richmond Seafood Landmark Since 1974, Listed for Sale
moreNews.body: Pacific Café — the 51-year-old Outer Richmond institution at 7000 Geary Blvd. known for its classic seafood plates, Boudin sourdough, and the rare tradition of pouring complimentary wine to waiting guests — is on the market as its co-owners, Frank Gundry and Ross Warren, prepare to retire. The restaurant is listed at $195,000 with annual revenues above $1 million; its owners say they hope to find a buyer willing to preserve its character. The café, which opened on July 4, 1974, is listed in San Francisco's Legacy Business Registry. Gundry and Warren have said they will remain open through the end of summer while the sale process continues, meaning diners can still visit Wednesday through Sunday from 5 to 9 p.m.

moreNews.headline: Maria Isabel, the Dalida Team's Upscale Mexican Restaurant, Earns Raves in Presidio Heights
moreNews.body: Maria Isabel, the contemporary Mexican restaurant opened in March 2026 by chef couple Laura and Sayat Ozyilmaz at 500 Presidio Ave. in Presidio Heights, has quickly established itself as one of San Francisco's most talked-about new dining destinations. The San Francisco Chronicle called it 'SF's most ambitious Mexican restaurant in years,' and The Infatuation gave it an 8.5 rating, praising dishes that draw from Laura Ozyilmaz's upbringing in Guerrero and weave in California ingredients including local uni, squid, and sourdough tortillas. The restaurant is open Tuesday through Saturday, 5 to 9:30 p.m., and seats 56 guests across two distinct rooms.

moreNews.headline: Presidio Gets New Board After Trump Ousted All Six Biden-Era Trustees
moreNews.body: Following President Trump's April dismissal of all six Biden-appointed Presidio Trust board members, the White House in May appointed an entirely new slate of six directors to oversee the 1,500-acre national park. The new board includes Lynne Benioff, who previously served as board chair and co-chaired the Presidio Tunnel Tops fundraising campaign; technology entrepreneur and former U.S. Ambassador to Austria Trevor Traina; Laura Arrillaga-Andreessen, a Stanford educator and Silicon Valley philanthropist; James Burnham, general counsel at xAI and X; real estate investor John Bickford; and Marine veteran Kyle Corcoran. The Presidio Trust has said day-to-day park operations continued uninterrupted throughout the transition.

moreNews.headline: Clement Street Cleanup Happy Hour Returns This Friday
moreNews.body: The Civic Joy Fund is hosting a Clement Street Happy Hour Cleanup this Friday, August 28, from 4 to 5 p.m., meeting at Richmond Republic Draught House at 642 Clement St. Volunteers are invited to help spruce up the neighborhood commercial corridor; supplies provided. The effort is part of a series of ongoing Richmond District cleanup days organized by the Civic Joy Fund throughout August and into fall.

restaurants.name: Rose Pizzeria
restaurants.description: Berkeley's nationally acclaimed thin-crust pizzeria, named one of America's best by the New York Times, opened its first San Francisco location on the prominent Clement and Arguello corner in 2026.

restaurants.name: Chapeau!
restaurants.description: Beloved family-run French bistro from chef-owner Philippe Gardelle serving classic escargots, coq au vin, and prix-fixe menus in a cozy Clement Street setting since 1996.

restaurants.name: Burma Superstar
restaurants.description: Iconic Burmese restaurant famous for its tea leaf salad and rainbow salad, drawing lines down Clement Street for decades.

restaurants.name: B Star
restaurants.description: Sister restaurant to Burma Superstar offering a more casual, bar-forward experience with many of the same beloved Burmese flavors plus cocktails.

restaurants.name: Arsicault Bakery
restaurants.description: Bon Appétit's best new bakery in America when it opened in 2015, Arsicault draws weekend lines stretching down Arguello for its supremely flaky croissants, kouign amann, and morning buns.

restaurants.name: Dalida
restaurants.description: Acclaimed restaurant from chef couple Laura and Sayat Ozyilmaz set on the Presidio's Main Parade Lawn, celebrated for its pillowy pita, tahdig, and Cypriot lamb chops with sweeping Alcatraz views.

restaurants.name: Maria Isabel
restaurants.description: Upscale Mexican restaurant from the Dalida team, drawing on chef Laura Ozyilmaz's Guerrero coastal upbringing with dishes like ceviche acapulqueño, sourdough tortillas, and seasonal California-sourced ingredients.

restaurants.name: Cinderella Russian Bakery
restaurants.description: A Richmond institution since 1953 serving piroshki, borscht, pelmeni, and Eastern European pastries to generations of neighborhood regulars.

restaurants.name: Mandalay Restaurant
restaurants.description: Long-standing Burmese restaurant on California Street celebrated for its ginger salad, mohinga fish noodle soup, and warm family-run hospitality.

restaurants.name: Kitchen Istanbul
restaurants.description: Intimate Clement Street restaurant offering Turkish and Eastern Mediterranean dishes including mezze, kebabs, and housemade baklava in a warmly decorated space.

restaurants.name: Pizzetta 211
restaurants.description: Tiny, reservation-free Outer Richmond spot turning out small-batch, seasonal thin-crust pizzas with a rotating menu of just a few options, beloved for its simplicity and quality.

restaurants.name: Mess Hall at Presidio Tunnel Tops
restaurants.description: The Presidio's newest dining destination, an all-day food hall adjacent to Tunnel Tops featuring a café serving Wrecking Ball Coffee, a full cocktail bar, three food concepts, and a retail market in a historic building with San Francisco Bay views.

restaurants.name: Pacific Café
restaurants.description: A 51-year-old Richmond institution at the corner of Geary and 34th Avenue, serving fresh seafood plates with Boudin sourdough and offering every waiting guest a complimentary glass of wine — a tradition since 1974.

restaurants.name: Plough and Stars
restaurants.description: Beloved Irish pub on Clement Street with live traditional music sessions most nights of the week and a warm neighborhood atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Richmond Republic Draught House
restaurants.description: Lively Clement Street craft beer bar with a rotating lineup of local and regional taps, a relaxed vibe, and a neighborhood gathering-spot feel.

restaurants.name: Toy Boat Dessert Café
restaurants.description: Charming dessert café filled with vintage tin toys, serving scoops of Clover ice cream, sodas, and espresso drinks to families and neighbors since 1979.

restaurants.name: Trad'r Sam
restaurants.description: Old-school Outer Richmond tiki bar open since 1937, serving strong, colorful cocktails in a kitschy, low-lit room beloved for its no-frills, time-warp atmosphere.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: A 22-room historic boutique hotel inside the Presidio, set in a restored Georgian Revival officers' building with complimentary continental breakfast, afternoon wine and cheese receptions, and fire-pit porches with Golden Gate views.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: A second Presidio Trust boutique hotel in a historic building on the Main Post, offering European-style breakfast buffets, afternoon wine and cheese, and a serene national park setting steps from Crissy Field.

shops.name: Green Apple Books & Music
shops.description: Beloved Richmond independent bookstore since 1967, with two Clement Street locations packed floor-to-ceiling with new and used books, music, and film; in 2026, the Sunset location opened its upstairs as a literary co-working space.

shops.name: Clement Street Farmers Market
shops.description: Year-round Sunday farmers market across three blocks of Clement Street in the Inner Richmond, featuring organic produce, baked goods, flowers, and specialty vendors from across the Bay Area.

shops.name: Sports Basement Presidio
shops.description: Large, well-priced outdoor and sporting goods retailer in the Presidio's historic Thoreau Center, carrying gear for hiking, cycling, camping, and watersports alongside apparel and rentals.

shops.name: Aroma Tea Shop
shops.description: Specialty tea shop on Clement Street with a vast selection of loose-leaf teas from China and Taiwan, teaware, and knowledgeable staff who guide customers through brewing techniques.

shops.name: Dragon's Gate Art
shops.description: Clement Street gallery and gift shop specializing in Asian art, ceramics, silk, and unique home goods sourced from across East and Southeast Asia.

shops.name: Lakeshore Natural Foods
shops.description: Community-focused natural foods market on California Street carrying organic produce, bulk goods, supplements, and specialty items for health-conscious Richmond shoppers.

shops.name: Park Life
shops.description: Celebrated Inner Richmond shop and small-press gallery combining design books, zines, art prints, and curated objects by local and international artists.

shops.name: Sloat Garden Center
shops.description: Full-service garden center on Geary Boulevard carrying a wide range of plants, soils, tools, and gardening supplies for Richmond residents and Golden Gate Park-adjacent gardeners.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: Forty-thousand-square-foot non-profit museum in the Presidio dedicated to the life and legacy of Walt Disney, with ten interactive galleries, over 200 video screens, early animations, personal artifacts, and a spectacular scale model of Disneyland.

artEntertainment.name: Legion of Honor
artEntertainment.description: Landmark fine arts museum in Lincoln Park at the edge of the Richmond, housing a permanent collection spanning 4,000 years of art alongside world-class traveling exhibitions including the current Etruscans show through September 20.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Theatre
artEntertainment.description: Restored 600-seat theater on the Presidio's Main Post hosting film screenings, live performances, community events, and — on September 17 — the world premiere of the Anza 250 documentary marking the park's 250th birthday.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
artEntertainment.description: Historic adobe building on the Presidio's Main Post housing free exhibitions including the ongoing EXCLUSION show on the WWII Japanese American incarceration, plus the Heritage Gallery tracing the park's 250-year history.

artEntertainment.name: ArtSeed at Tides Converge
artEntertainment.description: Presidio-based arts education nonprofit hosting free exhibitions in the China Brotsky and Seed Galleries, including the current 20th Annual Open Call Exhibition, 'So What Now?', running through September 18.

artEntertainment.name: Plough and Stars
artEntertainment.description: Clement Street Irish pub and live music institution hosting traditional music sessions most nights, making it one of the best spots in San Francisco for authentic acoustic Irish folk and trad.

artEntertainment.name: 4 Star Theater
artEntertainment.description: Independent cinema on Clement Street showing a mix of current releases, art house films, and free family-friendly weekend morning screenings in 2026.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Visitor Center
artEntertainment.type: National park visitor center and gallery
artEntertainment.description: The Presidio Trust's main visitor center offers free self-guided and ranger-led programming, rotating interpretive exhibitions, and serves as the starting point for exploring the park's 250 years of layered history.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: Historic public golf course in the Presidio, one of the most scenic on the West Coast, with fairways winding through cypress and eucalyptus groves with views of the Golden Gate Bridge.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Bowling Center
gymsRecreation.description: Twelve-lane bowling alley in the Presidio with a full grill menu, a selection of 45 beers and ciders, and open lanes for drop-in bowling, private events, and league play.

gymsRecreation.name: Rob Hill Campground
gymsRecreation.description: One of only two campgrounds in San Francisco, Rob Hill Campground in the Presidio is open April through October and bookable through recreation.gov, offering a true urban camping experience minutes from the city.
gymsRecreation.address: Washington Blvd at Immigrant Point Trail, Presidio

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Tunnel Tops
gymsRecreation.description: Expansive park above the Presidio Parkway tunnels with sweeping Golden Gate Bridge views, a campfire circle, playground, and event meadows hosting free community programs throughout summer.

gymsRecreation.name: Crissy Field
gymsRecreation.type: Restored tidal marsh and beachfront park
gymsRecreation.description: Iconic restored wetlands and beach along the Presidio waterfront offering walking and cycling on the Golden Gate Promenade, kite flying, windsurfing, and Golden Gate Bridge views.

gymsRecreation.name: Sports Basement Presidio — Rentals & Fitness
gymsRecreation.type: Outdoor gear rental and fitness events
gymsRecreation.description: The Presidio Sports Basement location hosts regular demo runs, fitness events, and rents bikes, camping, and outdoor gear, making it a hub for active Presidio visitors.

gymsRecreation.name: Mountain Lake Park
gymsRecreation.description: Peaceful park in the Inner Richmond/Lake Street neighborhood surrounding one of San Francisco's only remaining natural lakes, with a playground, walking paths, and restored wetland habitat.

gymsRecreation.name: Lincoln Park
gymsRecreation.description: Rugged headlands park in the Outer Richmond home to the Legion of Honor museum, the Land's End coastal trail with dramatic ocean and Golden Gate views, and the historic Sutro Baths ruins.

gymsRecreation.name: Ocean Beach
gymsRecreation.description: Three-mile stretch of Pacific Ocean beach bordering the Outer Richmond, popular for surfing, walking, bonfires in designated fire rings, and dramatic sunsets over the water.
